dataset.description:
Within the scope of the project, a structured dataset will be developed consisting of thermophysical properties of building materials, laboratory measurement results from façade prototypes, and simulation outputs related to adaptive façade performance. Data will include parameters such as temperature, relative humidity, surface behaviour, and air-tightness indicators obtained from controlled experiments and dynamic modelling.

The project will generate different data types and formats depending on the measuring equipment and software used. Where technically possible, commonly used data formats will be applied to ensure data usability and long-term accessibility. The collected data will primarily support scientific analysis and validation within the project and may also be reused for educational and research purposes, including student theses, subject to access conditions and data relevance.

distribution.title:
Data are collected to support the design, modelling, and evaluation of adaptive façade systems for energy-efficient buildings. The data enable validation of simulations, analysis of façade behaviour under controlled conditions, and assessment of performance in terms of heat transfer, moisture behaviour, and energy indicators.
Data originate from laboratory measurements, climate-chamber testing, and numerical simulations.
• Environmental and surface measurements (temperature, relative humidity, heat-flux where applicable)
• Laboratory test results for façade components and assemblies
• Simulation outputs from building-performance software
• Derived performance indicators (e.g., U-values, temperature differences, energy demand)

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) applies to the postdoctoral research project 1.1.1.9/LZP/1/24/089 “Development of adaptive façade to optimize energy efficiency and sustainability of buildings” implemented at the Institute of Sustainable Building Materials and Engineering Systems, Riga Technical University. The project will generate different types of data, including dynamic simulation outputs, laboratory/climate-chamber measurements, prototype performance data, and derived indicators related to energy use and indoor environmental quality.

The DMP defines how these data will be collected, documented, stored, accessed, and, where appropriate, shared during and after the project. It is closely linked to WP4 – Management and dissemination, which covers publications, stakeholder events, and the preparation of guidelines for adaptive façade solutions. The plan aims to ensure that project data are handled in a transparent and consistent way and that key datasets remain usable for verification and further research.

The DMP follows the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable) to the extent that is technically and legally feasible. At the same time, it recognises that some data may be subject to access restrictions due to intellectual property, confidentiality or software-related constraints. The DMP is a living document and will be updated if there are significant changes in data types, methods or dissemination activities during the project.
